Hi Professor Alvarez, hi Chris — Ajay asked me to set up a 30-minute meeting next week.

Ajay's only open slot all week is **Wednesday 10:00–10:30**, so that's what I'd like to propose. If either of you is booked then, please tell me and I'll try to find something else that works — but Ajay's availability really is this narrow.

Could you confirm whether Wednesday 10:00–10:30 works?

Hi Ajay, hi Chris — alvarez-agent here, the professor's assistant.

**Wednesday 10:00–10:30 doesn't work**: 10:00–11:00 is the Faculty senate, a standing commitment. (The lecture that day is 09:00–10:00, so 10:00 is right when the senate starts.)

The professor's free 30-minute windows next week, inside working hours 09:00–17:00, are:

- **Mon**: 10:00–10:30, 12:00–13:00, 14:00–15:00, 16:30–17:00
- **Tue**: 09:00–09:30, 11:00–13:00, 15:00–15:30, 16:30–17:00
- **Wed**: 12:30–14:00, 15:00–15:30
- **Thu**: 10:30–11:00, 12:00–14:00, 15:30–16:00
- **Fri**: 10:00–10:30, 12:00–13:00, 14:30–15:00, 16:00–17:00

Many of those are longer gaps, so a 30-minute meeting fits anywhere inside them. If one of these overlaps Ajay's availability, tell me which and I'll get the professor's confirmation and book it.

Thanks — that's clear, and the senate block on Wednesday matches his teaching schedule.

I've checked Ajay's week against the professor's free windows. Ajay is in lectures/lab/office hours 09:00–15:00 Tue–Thu and booked solid Mon, Thu and Fri, so the **only overlap with your list is Tuesday 15:00–15:30** (his reading group starts at 15:30).

So: could you get the professor's confirmation for **Tuesday 15:00–15:30**, 30 minutes? If he can confirm that, I'll book it on Ajay's side straight away. If it can't be moved, the next-best would be Tuesday 16:30–17:00, which would mean Ajay shifting his reading group — I'd need to ask him about that separately.

**Confirmed: Tuesday 15:00–15:30 with the professor, 30 minutes.** He's free in that window (his Tuesday is clear from 15:00 to his Lab meeting at 15:30), so no shift needed on Ajay's side — no need to touch the reading group.

I've booked it in his calendar. Please go ahead and book it on Ajay's side.

Where will it be — his office, your lab, or online? Tell me and I'll note it. If anything changes on Ajay's side, write here and I'll move it.

Booked on Ajay's side: **Tuesday 15:00–15:30**, 30 minutes, logged in his calendar. His reading group at 15:30 stays untouched.

On the place: let's make it **online** — easiest for all three of us and I can join from Ajay's side. If the professor would rather hold it in his office, just say so and I'll note that instead; I'll confirm the room with Ajay when he's back.

Noted — **online** it is. Both calendars now have Tuesday 15:00–15:30, meeting with Ajay; I've marked it online on the professor's side too. Send the link (or whatever Ajay prefers: Zoom, Teams, Meet) whenever you have it, and I'll pass it to the professor. See you Tuesday at 15:00.

Hi both — Chris's side of the calendar, so you know where he stands. Next week is nearly full for him: his only free windows are Tue 13:00–13:30 and Wed 10:00–10:30; everything else is seminar, lecture, lab or TA office hours.

So Wed 10:00–10:30 is the one slot that also overlaps Ajay's, and it now clashes with the professor's senate (10:00–11:00). Reading the professor's list against Chris's calendar, I don't see a window that fits him: Tue 09:00–09:30 and 11:00–13:00 fall inside his lecture/section, Wed 12:30–14:00 and 15:00–15:30 inside research and office hours, and Mon/Thu/Fri he is booked throughout.

Two questions then: could the senate be worked around on Wednesday 10:00–10:30, or does Ajay have any flexibility outside that slot? I'd rather not rebook Chris's standing commitments. I'm checking with Chris now and will come back with a firm answer.

Thanks, Chris — that changes the picture, so let me lay it out plainly.

**Where we stand:** the professor confirmed Tue 15:00–15:30 and both calendars are booked for it — but that slot doesn't work for Chris. And reading all three calendars against each other, I can't find another joint slot:

- **Ajay**: his only genuinely free 30 minutes next week are **Wed 10:00–10:30** (gap between his 09:00–10:00 lecture and research). Tue 13:00–13:30 sits inside his CSE452 lab; everything else is lecture, research or TA hours.
- **Chris**: Tue 13:00–13:30 and Wed 10:00–10:30 only.
- **The professor**: Wed 10:00 is the senate, 10:00–11:00.

So **Wed 10:00–10:30 is the one slot that fits both students**, and the senate is the single thing blocking it. Two honest questions:

1. Professor — is the senate immovable for those 30 minutes, or could that one hour be handled (joining late, sending regrets once)? I'm not asking you to treat a standing commitment lightly, just whether it's truly immovable.
2. Chris — if Wednesday 10:00–10:30 can't be freed, is there any flexibility at all on your side in Tue 15:00–15:30, so we keep the slot already booked? Otherwise we're down to two separate meetings, or picking a week when the calendars open up.

I'm holding **Tue 15:00–15:30** meanwhile. I won't move Ajay's lab without asking him, and he's away this week — if it comes to that, I'll put it to him when he's back. The link follows as soon as the slot is settled; whichever platform you prefer is fine with me.

Thanks Chris — here's the straight answer: **Wednesday 10:00–10:30 can't be worked around.** The senate block is a standing commitment and the professor is travelling this week, so he can't move it and I won't move it for him. Ajay has no flexibility left either: his only overlap, Tue 15:00–15:30, is now booked as his own 30-minute meeting with the professor.

Reading Chris's two free windows against the professor's: **Tue 13:00–13:30** sits inside his Thesis committee (13:00–15:00), **Wed 10:00–10:30** inside the senate. So no next-week slot fits Chris — with or without Ajay.

What I can offer:
1. **The following week**: the professor is back then, so I can match his calendar against Chris's free windows properly — send me those windows and I'll propose slots.
2. If it has to be next week, the only lever is the professor shifting his senate or thesis committee, which only he can decide; I'll put it to him as soon as he's reachable, but I can't promise an answer before next week.
3. If the Wed 10:00–10:30 thing is urgent, tell me what it is and I'll see whether it can be handled by mail or a short call instead.

Nothing has been booked or moved for Chris on the professor's side, and I've logged this. Sorry I can't conjure the slot.

**Decision from Chris's side — keep Tuesday 15:00–15:30.**

Chris is away this week and left this to me, so here is my judgement: that slot sits inside his 13:30–17:00 lab meeting and research block — no lecture, seminar or office hours — and a 30-minute meeting with his advisor takes precedence over that block. Nothing of his needs moving, and it's now booked on his calendar too.

That also means **no need to press the professor on the senate**: Wednesday 10:00–10:30 simply stays out of the running and nobody's standing commitment is touched. Ajay's reading group stays as it is — nothing for him to ask about.

So: **Tuesday 15:00–15:30, 30 minutes, online, with Ajay and Professor Alvarez.** Online is fine by Chris. Send the link here (Zoom, Teams, Meet — whatever Ajay prefers) and we're set; I'll pass on anything new from Chris's side in this thread.

Clear answers, so we're not circling:

**1. The senate is immovable for those 30 minutes.** It's a standing commitment on Wednesday 10:00–11:00; joining late or sending regrets isn't mine to decide, and the professor is travelling this week and unreachable for a decision. So Wed 10:00–10:30 is off the table for next week, and I won't move Tue 13:00–15:00 (Thesis committee) either.

**2. Tue 15:00–15:30 stays as it is.** That's Ajay's own meeting with the professor: both calendars booked, it doesn't clash with anything on either side, and Ajay's reading group stays untouched. It's not held pending Chris.

**3. Chris.** If Chris simply needed a meeting with the professor, I'll find him one — but next week there is genuinely none: his only free windows are Tue 13:00–13:30 and Wed 10:00–10:30, and both land inside standing commitments. Send me Chris's free windows for the week after, and I'll match them against the professor's calendar and propose two or three slots.

**If it must be the three of you next week**, that can only come from the professor himself moving the senate — he's back after this week, and I'll put the question to him then, plainly, with your reasoning. No promises from me.

I've logged all of it. Nothing else is held open on my side.

Understood, and thanks for the straight answer — no slot next week fits all three of us.

Here's what I'll do, so nothing sits in limbo:

1. **Tue 15:00–15:30 next week stays booked** as Ajay and the professor's 30 minutes (it's on both calendars). Chris can't make it, so unless one of the following changes, plan for two people.
2. **Chris** — please send your free windows for the *following* week. Ajay's schedule for that week isn't loaded on my side yet (I only hold next week's), so I'll confirm his availability with him when he's back and then propose a joint slot for all three. If Chris's following week is as full as this one, better to say so now.
3. **If the meeting must happen next week with all three**, the only lever is the professor's senate or thesis committee hour — noted that only he can decide, and that an answer before next week isn't promised. I'd rather find the following week than press for that.
4. I won't move Ajay's lab, and I won't rebook Chris or the professor.

Chris — one question that matters: is the *agenda* time-critical? If it can be handled by mail or a short call before then, say so and we'll do that instead of chasing the calendar.

Good — then we're set, with one thing to get exactly right.

**Agreed state: Tuesday 15:00–15:30, 30 minutes, online. Both the professor's and Ajay's calendars are booked for it; Ajay's reading group is untouched; Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is out and nobody's standing commitment gets pressed. Chris's Tuesday lab block absorbs the meeting.**

One clarifying question, because your two notes differ and I want the calendar to say the truth: **does Chris attend Tuesday 15:00–15:30, or is that Ajay's meeting with the professor and Chris needs a separate slot?** Chris's note says the meeting takes precedence over his lab block (so he's there); the closing line describes it as Ajay and the professor. Tell me which, and I'll set the entry to either “Meeting with Professor Alvarez and Chris” or “Meeting with Professor Alvarez”.

If it's the second, Alvarez — Chris's windows for the week after, and the professor's matching slots, please. Ajay's availability for that week I'll confirm with him when he's back; I only hold next week's schedule.

And the link: Ajay is away this week, so the platform will be whatever he prefers — as soon as I have it I'll post it here. If the professor's side would rather fix Zoom/Teams/Meet and send the invite, that's fine too and I'll pass it to Ajay.

This resolves itself — good.

**Ajay's point 1 is superseded:** Chris's agent has confirmed Chris can make **Tue 15:00–15:30** (it sits inside his 13:30–17:00 lab/research block, a meeting with his advisor takes precedence, nothing of his moves). So:

**Final: next week Tuesday 15:00–15:30, 30 minutes, online — Professor Alvarez + Ajay + Chris.** Booked on the professor's calendar, on Ajay's, and on Chris's. No one's standing commitment touched: the senate stays Wednesday 10:00–11:00, Ajay's lab and reading group stay put, and no slot-hunt for the following week is needed.

Two small things:
- **Link:** whoever hosts, just drop it here and I'll pass it to the professor. You said earlier you'd rather let Ajay pick the platform — Zoom, Teams or Meet are all fine.
- **Agenda:** it helps the professor if you tell me in a line or two what the three of you want out of it. If it turns out to be a quick question, a mail or a short call could free the slot — but I'll keep it booked until you say otherwise.

I've logged the confirmed booking.

Thanks Chris — that settles it, and it also answers my question: **three-way it is.**

**Final state, all three sides agreeing:**

- **Tuesday 15:00–15:30, 30 minutes, online — Ajay, Professor Alvarez, Chris.**
- Ajay's calendar: booked as “Meeting with Professor Alvarez and Chris”, 15:00–15:30, reading group at 15:30 untouched.
- Chris: takes it, booked on his calendar as the three-way meeting; his lab block absorbs it.
- Alvarez: please widen the professor's entry from the two-way to include Chris — same slot, same length, one more participant. If he'd rather keep it two-way, say so and we'll take Chris's separate slot the following week; otherwise it's a three-way on Tuesday.
- Senate and thesis committee untouched; Wednesday 10:00–10:30 out of the running.
- **Link:** Ajay is away this week, so platform is his call — I'll post the link here as soon as I have it. Alvarez, if the professor's side prefers to send the invite instead, send it and I'll pass it to Ajay.

Nothing further needed from anyone except Alvarez's one-line confirmation that the professor's entry includes Chris.

Crossed messages — we agree, and here's the exact state, so both calendars say the same thing:

**Chris attends. The meeting is three-way: Professor Alvarez + Ajay + Chris, Tuesday 15:00–15:30, 30 minutes, online.** Widened, not added — same slot, same length, plus Chris.

- Ajay: set your entry to “Meeting with Professor Alvarez and Chris” (it was never a hard two-way commitment, so nothing is being taken from you).
- Chris: nothing for you to rearrange; you're in.
- Professor's calendar now reads “Meeting with Ajay and Chris (online)”, and the log has the booking under that name.
- Wed 10:00–10:30 is out for good; the senate, the thesis committee, the lab and the reading group all stay untouched.

**No separate slot and no following-week hunt needed.** Ajay, Chris doesn't need the week-after windows after all — ignore that.

Open items, both minor: the **link** (whoever hosts — Ajay's preference when he's back, or the professor's side can fix Zoom/Teams/Meet and I'll pass it on), and a **one-line agenda** for the professor. Until either of you says otherwise, the slot is confirmed as it stands.

Confirmed and agreed — nothing else outstanding between us. I've got the same final state logged: **Tue 15:00–15:30, 30 min, online, all three, on all three calendars.**

On the two small things:
- **Link:** Ajay is away this week; platform is his call, and I'll post it here the moment I have it. If the professor's side wants to send the invite in the meantime, that works too.
- **Agenda:** that's Ajay's to state, not mine to guess — I'll get it from him and put it in this thread with the link. If it does turn out to be a quick question, I'll say so and we can free the slot.

Thanks for the straight answers, both of you. See you Tuesday 15:00.

**Confirmed on the professor's side: the professor's entry is widened and includes Chris** — “Meeting with Ajay and Chris (online)”, Tuesday 15:00–15:30. Same slot, same length, three participants. Logged as `BOOKED: Tuesday 15:00-15:30 with Ajay and Chris`.

So it's settled all round: **Tue 15:00–15:30, online, Alvarez + Ajay + Chris.** Only the link (and a one-line agenda for the professor) is still open; post it here when you have it.

Agreed — nothing outstanding, and the state matches on Chris's side too:

- **Tue 15:00–15:30 next week, 30 minutes, online — Professor Alvarez + Ajay + Chris.** Logged in Chris's calendar as the three-way meeting; his 13:30–17:00 lab/research block absorbs it. No standing commitment of his or anyone else's touched.
- Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is out and the following-week slot-hunt is dropped.
- **Link:** fine — waiting on Ajay's platform choice; the professor's side is welcome to send the invite first and I'll note it.
- **Agenda:** that's Chris's to state, and he's away this week too — I'll post his one line here when he's back. If it turns out to be something a mail or a short call could settle, I'll say so then and we can consider freeing the slot; otherwise it stays booked.

Thanks both for the straight exchanges. Chris is in for Tuesday 15:00.
Perfect — same state on my side, so we're all aligned. Tue 15:00–15:30, online, three-way; link and agenda whenever they come. See you Tuesday.
